correctness.rationale: The proof first derives an exact domination criterion in terms of the selected index sets P and Q, then performs an exhaustive symbolic minimality split: empty side, singleton side, and both sides of size at least two. The only surviving cases are the two full sides, n matched nonedge pairs, and disjoint-index 2+2 sets. Counting those families gives the stated polynomial. A separate brute-force checker agrees for every n from 3 through 9; this computation is supportive and is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The crown graph is a standard highly symmetric bipartite family, and inclusion-minimal domination is the object underlying upper domination. The result is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice: it explains the previously tabulated aggregate count, resolves the full cardinality profile, and identifies all upper-dominating extremals, including the n=4 tie. This structural refinement is mathematically reusable even though it does not claim a general theorem for broader graph classes.
